known_facts_book1: Lives on a poor farm in Kansas with her Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, whose mortgaged farm is about to be taken from them.
Has been made a Princess of Oz by Ozma and is Ozma's chosen companion and faithful friend.
Asks Ozma to let her live in Oz and to bring Uncle Henry and Aunt Em there too, to escape losing the Kansas farm.
Ozma transports Dorothy, then her uncle and aunt, to the Emerald City by means of the Magic Belt.
Tours the odd corners of Oz in the Wizard's red wagon drawn by the Sawhorse, with Aunt Em, Uncle Henry, the Shaggy Man, Omby Amby and the Wizard.
Wanders off in a forest with Toto and Billina and gets lost, then visits Utensia, Bunbury and Bunnybury before the Wizard finds her.
Is captured by the Spoon Brigade and tried before King Kleaver in Utensia.
Lunches with the unhappy Rabbit King of Bunnybury and talks him out of abandoning his throne.
Proposes using the Magic Belt to wish everyone to Kansas and sell emeralds to pay the mortgage, a plan Ozma refuses.
Signs her farewell note to the author 'Dorothy Gale' on a stork's-wing feather at the book's end.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: Her dearest friend and the Ruler of Oz, who makes her a Princess and grants her wish to live in Oz with her uncle and aunt.
known_relations_book1.Aunt Em: Her aunt, brought from Kansas to live permanently in Oz.
known_relations_book1.Uncle Henry: Her uncle, brought from Kansas to live permanently in Oz.
known_relations_book1.Toto: Her little dog, who accompanies her everywhere and gets lost with her in the forest.
known_relations_book1.Billina: The Yellow Hen, an old friend from Ev, who is lost in the forest with her and shares her town adventures.
known_relations_book1.Nome King: Her enemy Roquat, who plots to conquer Oz and enslave her; she does not know of the danger until late.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Travelling companion who works Glinda's magic on the tour and finally tracks Dorothy's footprints to find her.
known_relations_book1.Shaggy Man: A companion on the wagon tour who has also 'been lost many a time.'
